question: Which output-length contract is robust across cheap method families without using a method-specific floor to hide selector collapse?
candidate_rationale: legacy_floor_200_cap_250 is the historical control and is not presumed valid.
median_cap_220 rounds the frozen dev median to an explainable ten-word cap.
max_only_250 isolates removal of the method-specific floor while preserving the historical ceiling.
p75_cap_260 uses the exact frozen dev p75 and tests whether the 250 ceiling is unnecessarily restrictive.
cheap_methods: lexical-only provenance-aware deterministic Greedy with length_normalized importance
controlled_components: same canonical rows and frozen partition
same candidate/objective settings within the Greedy method

selection_rule.dev: Run all four protocols and all three methods; rank by the mean across methods of per-document macro mean(ROUGE-1, ROUGE-2, ROUGE-Lsum).
selection_rule.dev_test: Evaluate every still-valid protocol exactly once. Select the highest mean cross-method macro ROUGE only if paired 95% bootstrap differences versus every alternative exclude zero after Holm correction.
selection_rule.tie: If no protocol has a multiplicity-corrected advantage, freeze max_only_250 because it changes only the unjustified lower floor and preserves the established, easily explained upper ceiling.
selection_rule.rejection: Reject any protocol with row loss, schema drift, upper-budget violation, or different evaluation denominator. Report infeasibility rather than relaxing fail-loud.

govreport.rule: After canonical GovReport validation and its partition are frozen, instantiate the same four protocol roles using that dataset's frozen dev median/p75 and historical official cap if one exists. Do not transplant Multi-News word values.
govreport.finalization: A1 is not globally complete until GovReport runs the same preregistered rule. Dataset-specific numeric caps are allowed; the rule family must remain fixed.
